title: Grip, cocking and lowering the hammer
subtitle: Holding the handgun the same way, every time

lines: This episode covers the grip, cocking the revolver, and lowering the hammer under control.
The book says it is important to grip the firearm the same way every time you shoot.

scenes.heading: The grip
bullets: Like a handshake: firm but comfortable
Barrel in line with the forearm
Pistol: web of the hand snugly under the tang
Trigger finger alongside the trigger guard
lines: Many new shooters have a tendency to hold the gun too tightly.

lines.text: The grip on the firearm should be similar to a handshake, firm but comfortable.
When the firearm is held correctly, the barrel should be in line with the forearm.
On a semi-automatic pistol, the web of the hand should fit snugly under the tang.
You should have three fingers around the grip.
One finger, your trigger finger, goes alongside the trigger guard.
And your thumb goes on the opposite side of the firearm.

scenes.heading: One handed grip: pistol
scenes.caption: One handed grip, and a top view of it
lines: Here you see the correct grip, with the web of the hand fitting snugly under the tang.
On the right is a top view of the same one handed grip.

scenes.heading: One handed grip: revolver
scenes.caption: One handed grip on a revolver
lines: And this is the one handed grip on a revolver.
Again, the trigger finger lies alongside the trigger guard.

scenes.heading: The support hand
bullets: Heel of the support hand onto the grip
Four fingers around the strong hand's fingers
Both thumbs on the same side
Do not place support thumb behind the slide
lines: Now, the support hand.

lines.text: Place the heel of the support hand onto the grip, between the fingertips and the heel of the strong hand.
Wrap the four fingers of your support hand around the strong hand's fingers.
Keep both thumbs on the same side of the firearm.
Do not place your support hand thumb behind the slide.

rule.text: Grip the firearm the same way every time you shoot.

lines: It is important to grip the firearm the same way every time you shoot.
You should not have to adjust your grip between shots.

scenes.heading: Two handed grip: pistol
scenes.caption: Steps 1 and 2 of the two handed grip
lines: The book shows four steps to the correct two handed grip on a semi-automatic pistol.
In step one, the strong hand grips the pistol, and the support hand is open beside it.
In step two, the heel of the support hand comes onto the grip.

scenes.heading: Two handed grip: pistol
scenes.caption: Steps 3 and 4 of the two handed grip
lines: In step three, the support hand fingers wrap around the strong hand's fingers, with both thumbs on the same side.
Step four shows the completed two handed grip from the other side.

scenes.heading: Two handed grip: revolver
scenes.caption: The three steps of the two handed grip on a revolver
lines: For the revolver, the book shows three steps.
One: the strong hand grips the revolver, and the open support hand comes in from below.
Two: the heel of the support hand is placed against the grip.
Three: the support hand fingers wrap around the strong hand's fingers, completing the grip.

lines.text: Now, cocking the revolver. This is the hammer.
Cocking means pulling the hammer all the way back.

scenes.heading: Cocking the revolver
scenes.caption: Correct: the thumb of the support hand
lines: When cocking the revolver, use the thumb of the support hand to pull the hammer all the way back.
In the first photo, the support hand thumb reaches up to the hammer, and in the second, it pulls it back.

scenes.heading: The incorrect way
scenes.caption: Incorrect: the thumb of the gun hand
lines: This is the incorrect way.
Never use the thumb of the gun hand to cock the revolver.
This will cause you to lose proper grip, and therefore lose control of the firearm.

scenes.heading: Lowering the hammer under control
bullets: Apply pressure in front of the hammer
Slowly lower it, hand supported on top
Don't release until it's all the way forward
lines: The book's three steps will enable you to safely lower the hammer on the firearm.

lines.text: One: when lowering the hammer, always apply pressure in front of the hammer.
Two: slowly lower the hammer, using pressure from the front.

lines: Notice that the hand is supported by placing it on top of the firearm.

lines.text: Three: do not release the hammer until it is all the way forward.

scenes.heading: Lowering the hammer
scenes.caption: The three steps of lowering the hammer under control
lines: Here are those three steps in the book's photos.
Remember that if the hammer slips out of your fingers, the gun will fire.

scenes.question: If you are right handed, which thumb should cock the revolver's hammer?
options: Right thumb, on the gun hand
Left thumb, on the support hand
lines: Here's a question from your formative exam.
If you are right handed, which thumb should be used to cock the hammer on the revolver?
reveal: The thumb of the support hand, so for a right handed shooter, the left thumb.
Never use the thumb of the gun hand, as this will cause you to lose proper grip and control of the firearm.

scenes.question: How should the grip on the firearm feel?
options: Like a handshake, firm but comfortable
Loose, so the gun can move
lines: One more.
How should the grip on the firearm feel?
reveal: Similar to a handshake, firm but comfortable.
Many new shooters have a tendency to hold the gun too tightly.

points: Barrel in line with the forearm
Both thumbs on the same side
Cock with the support hand thumb
Lower the hammer with pressure from the front
lines: So, grip like a handshake, firm but comfortable.
Held correctly, the barrel is in line with the forearm.
With two hands, both thumbs stay on the same side, and never behind the slide.
Cock the revolver with the thumb of the support hand.
And lower the hammer slowly, with pressure from the front, until it's all the way forward.
